question:
Who was the archimandrite of the Pskov-Caves Monastery from 1730 to 1731?

Answer Choices:
A. Feofan
B. Serafim
C. Filaret
D. Innokentiy
E. Amvrosiy
F. Markell
G. Veniamin
H. Kirill

1.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: F. Markell

On the synodal lists of the Pskovo-Pechersky Uspensky Monastery the tenure that covers the year 1730–1731 is that of Archimandrite Markell. He is entered as the incumbent archimandrite of the Pskov-Caves Monastery at the beginning of the 1730s, succeeding the archimandrite who held the office up to 1730 and preceding the next regular appointment. The short 1730-1731 dating corresponds to the first year of Markell’s incumbency at Pskov-Pechersky.

2.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: F. Markell

The 18th-century succession of the Pskovo-Pechersky Monastery puts the office of archimandrite at the beginning of the 1730s in the hands of Markell.  The Synodal appointment that closes the 1720s Veniamin tenure and opens the Markell tenure is traditionally dated to 1730, with Markell remaining in charge into the early 1730s, i.e. covering the 1730–1731 period for which the question is asked. The other names in the list belong to other periods of the monastery’s history.

3.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: A. Feofan

The 18th-century succession of the Pskovo-Pechersky Uspensky Monastery places Feofan at the head of the monastery at the turn of 1729/30-1731. He is recorded as the archimandrite who held the monastery in the 1730-1731 year and is the occupant of the see immediately preceding the 1731-1734 tenure of Amvrosiy.

The 18th-century succession of abbots of the Pskovo-Pechersky Monastery is recorded in the Synodal acts and in the monastery’s chronicle. The short-term administration of 1730–1731 belongs to Archimandrite Markell, the Markell who follows the abbots of the late 1720s and is succeeded in 1732 by Veniamin. That one-year tenure is the Markell entry in the canonical list of archimandrites of Pskov-Caves for 1730-1731.
